predictions.reasoning: A sharp jump in the implied probability of Xi being removed from power signals acute Chinese political-succession risk. Leadership instability at the very top of the CCP raises policy-uncertainty premia, threatens continuity of economic and regulatory policy, and would trigger a rapid de-risking of Chinese equity exposure by global investors. FXI is a liquid, broadly-traded proxy for the offshore/large-cap China complex and would be among the first vehicles hit. The distribution is highly asymmetric: a credible signal could produce a >1500bps gap-down, but noise-driven spikes typically fade with little cash-market impact.

predictions.reasoning: Political-succession shock would prompt capital-flight fears and pressure on the yuan, weakening CNH (USD/CNH higher). CNH is more freely traded than onshore CNY and reacts fastest to China-risk headlines. Direction (CNH weaker) is our expectation, though the PBoC's heavy fixing management damps and can even reverse moves, and some scenarios (perceived reformist transition) could be read as neutral, hence lower confidence and wide band.

evidence_used: Market question implies probability of Xi's removal from power before 2027
Xi is central to Chinese policy continuity; succession is opaque and unpriced
FXI and USD/CNH are the most liquid, China-sensitive public-market proxies
Prediction-market spikes in low-probability political events are frequently rumor-driven and revert
uncertainty_notes: Base rate of a genuine leak vs noise in this market is very low; most spikes will be rumor
Direction is not unambiguous — markets could interpret a transition as neutral or even reform-positive
PBoC intervention can suppress or reverse FX moves regardless of the underlying signal
12h window may not capture cash-session reaction if signal occurs during illiquid hours

llm_justification.summary: A sharp rise in the implied probability that Xi Jinping is removed from power would most plausibly manifest as China risk-off: lower Chinese equities (FXI) and a weaker offshore yuan (higher USD/CNH). The reaction is highly asymmetric and event-conditional — a credible, corroborated signal could drive >1000bps equity moves, but the overwhelming likelihood is that any spike is rumor-driven and fades, so confidence is moderate and intervals are wide. FXI is the cleanest liquid proxy; CNH captures the capital-flight channel but is muted by PBoC management.
key_assumptions: The prediction-market probability actually moved sharply and precedes public confirmation
Investors read Xi-removal as destabilizing rather than neutral/positive
FXI and CNH remain liquid and tradable during the window
No immediate official denial neutralizes the signal
failure_modes: The spike is rumor/manipulation on an illiquid market and fully reverses within hours
News was already public and priced, leaving no residual move
Market interprets leadership change as policy-positive, flipping equity direction to up
PBoC intervention neutralizes CNH depreciation, breaking the FX proxy
Move occurs off-hours and 12h window closes before cash markets react
Weak proxy exposure: FXI/CNH may under-react relative to onshore A-shares that foreigners cannot easily trade
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
